name: Liquid ETF Core
description: First expanded daily ETF universe for multi-asset research, defensive rotation, sector leadership, risk-on/risk-off tests, and campaign discovery.

research_boundary.why_etfs_first: Liquid ETFs are easier to fetch, align, and reason about with the current daily backtester than individual stocks. They reduce survivorship-bias and delisting issues while still expanding beyond SPY-only timing.
research_boundary.data_policy: Fetch each symbol with quant-lab fetch using adjusted daily yfinance data and keep the generated provenance sidecar beside the ignored cache CSV.

benchmark.role: default buy-and-hold benchmark for US risk-asset comparisons

groups.rationale: Broad US equity exposures for baseline risk-on comparisons and index leadership tests.
Sector ETFs allow leadership, defensive-sector, and regime-rotation hypotheses without individual-stock universe maintenance.
Treasury, aggregate bond, and cashlike ETFs give defensive alternatives for drawdown-control and risk-off switching tests.
Gold, silver, oil, and broad commodities broaden inflation, crisis, and non-equity diversification hypotheses.
Developed, emerging, Japan, and Europe ETFs support global leadership and diversification tests with simple daily data.

known_caveats: ETF inception dates differ; use data-trust reports to inspect actual overlapping rows before portfolio runs.
Adjusted yfinance OHLCV is convenient but still depends on provider semantics; keep adjusted-price audits separate from strategy conclusions.
Commodity ETFs such as USO may have structural roll costs and product changes; conclusions are about the ETF product, not spot commodities.
This universe is liquid and institutionally visible, so it is useful for engine expansion but not yet the small-capacity niche layer.
